Of course.  Here’s a recipe for bourekas, a savory pastry that traditionally is made with phyllo dough.  I’ve adapted the recipe to use graham cracker crumbs instead of phyllo dough, which makes it much easier to work with.  You will need to prepare the graham cracker crumbs in a food processor or grinder ahead of time.
 
Ingredients

4 cups graham cracker crumbs

2 1/2 cups cold, unsalted butter, cut into small pieces

3 large eggs

2 teaspoons finely grated orange zest

2 tablespoons orange juice

1/2 teaspoon salt

1/4 teaspoon black pepper

1.  In the food processor, combine the graham cracker crumbs, butter, eggs, orange zest, orange juice, salt, and pepper.  Process to combine thoroughly.  The mixture will be sticky.  If it seems too sticky, scrape the sides and bottom of the food processor to make sure all the ingredients are mixed well.

2.  Line a baking sheet with parchment paper or silicone baking mat.  Pat the mixture into a 12-inch by 16-inch rectangle about 1/4-inch thick.

3.  Cut the pastry into 1/2-inch thick slices.  Place these on the prepared baking sheet, leaving a little space between each one so that they will overlap in the center.  Brush the tops with the egg mixture, then sprinkle with some more of the chopped orange zest and black pepper.

4.  Bake in the preheated oven for 15 to 20 minutes, or until lightly golden on the top.  Remove from the oven and let cool completely on the baking sheet.

5.  Serve warm or chilled.

I hope you enjoy this recipe as much as I do!
